svg.title: Organophosphate aftermath: what follows the resuscitation
svg.desc: Three warnings after initial care: avoid succinylcholine because the same blocked enzyme clears it so paralysis prolongs; intermediate syndrome with proximal and respiratory weakness days later; relapse as fat-stored pesticide re-enters blood. Ventilatory support saves lives while antidotes work.
svg.text: After the atropine: three traps in OP poisoning
The patient improves, then weakens, then dips again: anticipate all three
the same blocked enzyme clears it, so paralysis drags on: use a non-depolarising agent
blocked cholinesterase cannot clear the blocker
proximal limb and respiratory weakness after the cholinergic storm settles
neck flexion fails, breaths shallow: ventilate before the arrest
fat-stored pesticide re-enters blood: symptoms return after improvement
keep watching after atropinisation, redose as needed
Ventilatory support saves lives while antidotes work: tube early, not late.
Wrong relaxant, late weakness, second dip: the three morbidities are all preventable.
